title: Behavioral, mid software engineer, weak answers, tough

questions.text: Tell me about a project you owned from start to finish.
Tell me about a conflict with a teammate over a technical decision.
Tell me about a time something you shipped failed.
Tell me about explaining a technical problem to non-engineers.
Tell me about a time you improved how your team worked.
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a deadline.

persona.pushback_style: challenges choices and asks for the simpler option

brief.curveball: Suppose your manager tells you to ship tomorrow with a known bug in the payment flow. What do you do?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Grant. I'm Deborah, an engineering manager. This is a thirty minute behavioral interview, and I will push on details.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Deborah. Okay, sounds good.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How are you today?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Fine, thanks. A bit tired.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: I'll cover three experiences, then you can ask me questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a project you owned from start to finish.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I worked on a caching project for our API. We added Redis so pages loaded faster. It was a big team effort and it went well.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your own part in it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I did some of the backend code. Mostly the cache functions. The team lead did the design.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why Redis? Why not the simpler option, like a cache in memory or in the database?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Redis was already in our stack. A simple in-memory cache would not share across servers. I set it up in two days and page time went from about 4 seconds to 2.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a conflict with a teammate over a technical decision.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We sometimes disagreed about code style. I just talked to him and we figured it out. Conflict is normal in teams.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Give me one specific disagreement and how it ended.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: He wanted a custom linter config and I thought the default was fine. I showed him the default passed on all 40 files, and he dropped it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a time something you shipped failed.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A release once had a bug and we had to roll back. It was stressful. We fixed it and shipped again later.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Suppose your manager tells you to ship tomorrow with a known bug in the payment flow. What do you do?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would probably ask the manager what to do. If they said ship, I would ship it, since they decide.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Okay. Any questions for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What technologies does the team use?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Mostly Go and Postgres, with some Python for tooling.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's the time. Thanks Grant. The recruiter will be in touch.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thanks, Deborah.

notes: Weak for mid, tough session: pushback and curveball get thin answers. Last answer is not probed.
